newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell Nigeria says 18 staff freed, 109 still detained.
newsitem.headline: Shell Nigeria says 18 staff freed, 109 still detained.

text.p: Oil giant Shell said on Tuesday that 18 of its staff and contractors held in Nigeria by feuding communities have been freed.
A company spokesman told Reuters in Lagos that 109 staff and contractors were still being detained at Shell's six flow stations which the villagers have occupied since weekend.
Two of those freed had injuries and all had been held hostage by villagers in the Niger Delta protesting over the relocation of their local government headquarters.
"Of the 18 released, two of them were among the six injured on Saturday. Our supply boat left at midday today to pick the injured based on an accord reached with the villagers," the spokesman added.
The company said on Tuesday that three people were injured on Monday night at one of the pumping stations in a fresh skirmish with the villagers.

The weekend attack made Shell shut down operations in the six stations and forced it to cut back production by 100,000 barrels per day of crude, about five percent of Nigeria's total output of almost two million bpd.
The Shell spokesman said the output cut had not affected crude exports and supply commitments, adding: "We will continue to negotiate with the villagers until all those held are eventually released."
